chunks: Muhammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muhammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muhammad ibn al-Faḍl, who said:

I said to al-Riḍā (peace be upon him): A man purchased a debt owed by another man, then he went to the debtor and said to him: Pay me what so-and-so owes you, for I have purchased it from him. He (al-Riḍā) said: 'He pays him the value of what he paid to the debtor, and the one upon whom the money is due is cleared of all that remains of his debt.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling a debt and how is the debtor discharged?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes the principle of 'bay' al-dayn' (sale of debt), clarifying that when a debt is sold, the original debtor pays the purchase price to the new creditor and is fully discharged, regardless of any discount or premium. This ruling highlights the transferability of financial obligations in Shia jurisprudence and ensures the debtor's liability is fixed at the transaction value rather than the face value. It serves as a foundational text for commercial transactions involving receivables in Islamic finance.
